Episode 138: The Keeper of the White Night Tower (7)
'Is that the ship of Kinzello, who withstood the sword of the Black Emperor? Was the name Gruenil?'
As soon as Hedo confirmed the ship, he felt a surge of irritation. Thick blood vessels swelled angrily over his rugged muscles.
Ever since entering the transcendent realm as a martial artist, Hedo had never experienced such a frustrating situation. His skills had always simplified complex matters.
Now it was the opposite. A simple task of saving Jin and Murakan had become tangled like a knotted thread.
Nothing went as planned.

The vault was suddenly robbed, Jin kept resisting despite Hedo's attempts to save him with a strangely sly tongue, it turned out Yona had robbed the vault and was injured by the sword, Sandra impatiently broke the ceiling by herself, and now Kinzello's ship was causing trouble.
It was even ridiculous that the Gruenil ship appeared at this moment.
'At this rate, it'll look like I requested support from my family not because of the Lun Kandels, but undoubtedly because of Kinzello.'
Sighing and smoothing his white hair, Hedo suddenly thought that maybe this side would be less troublesome in many ways.
'Well, explaining to the head of the family that I requested support just because I couldn't handle these intruders might have been more of a headache. Maybe it's for the best?'
From Hedo's point of view, hundreds of black dots spread across the dark dawn sky behind the Lun Kandels.

They were the dragons of Drakka, carrying the magicians and flying towards them. Among them, the flagship Cojack shone brightly, likely with Octavia as the commander on board. If Kelliak had not been absent, he would have taken Octavia's place.
Hedo's request for support meant that. That even he alone couldn't handle the situation, and the family needed to be on alert.
'How ridiculous. Maybe it's time to shed the shell of pride and arrogance once more.'
Hedo chuckled and lowered his head.
He found it amusing how complacent he had been, thinking himself strong. Even the invincible and unapproachable Siron Lun Kandel would never have been complacent in a situation like this.
"Huh? What's that, Gruenil? It's firing cannons at our fleet?"
Sandra said.
Boom...!
Cannons were fired from all around Gruenil. The anchored ships began to be mercilessly destroyed.
The majestic flames drove away the darkness like gods playing with fireworks, and the burning debris raining down looked like a meteor shower.

If the general public had seen this, they would think that the powerful fleet was collapsing. It was obvious when considering how astronomical the manpower and resources invested in building such a fleet were.
However, the Lun Kandels swallowed their dry saliva, seized by an unpleasant premonition that even this would not deal a terrible blow to the mighty organization Ziepel.
They felt as if they were only truly experiencing the might of the world's number one enemy, Ziepel, after participating in this mission.

"Hedo! If we save them all like this, it'll increase Jin's chances of survival! The headquarters will surely think that Hedo requested support not because of the Lun Kandels, but because of Gruenil. Isn't that right? Honestly, it's absurd for Hedo to request support from the headquarters just because of these intruders."
Whether it was true or not, Sandra's voice was bright. This fact made the Lun Kandels' hearts feel even more suffocated.
"So let's save them all, open the way! Hurry up and move, or I'll rip your mouth in a cross, you incompetent muscle pig!"
As Sandra shouted again, Hedo made eye contact with Jin once more.
'You really have luck on your side, Jin Runecandel.'
Hedo reached a conclusion, and for a moment, Jin looked into his inner thoughts.
He instinctively understood the look in Hedo's eyes as he thought of Siron, shedding his arrogance and resolving to enter a higher realm of martial arts.
It was a look that only someone who had gone through such determination could understand.
'Next time we meet, will you be even stronger there? Can you do it, tower guardian?'
A shiver ran down his spine.
He needed to be prepared. Before that monster transcended once more, he and the Runecandels had to achieve even more dazzling growth.
Pa-chi-ching-!

Suddenly, the longsword veil produced a sharp metallic sound and turned a pale white. Hedo swung the veil in the blink of an eye, and the Runecandels barely managed to react and take a defensive stance.
However, the wave of sword energy didn't even touch the Runecandels. Instead, it reached behind them and the upper part of the magic tower.
"No, don't!"
"Hedo, oh, oh... ah... ah...!"
The target of his sword energy was the wraiths clinging to the Tower of Eternal Night, gasping for breath.
It was like a wave of light.
The wraiths were disassembled like coarse salt under the aura of Hedo's swordsmanship and scattered outside the cracks in the tower.
The wraiths' final screams faded away like distant echoes, powerless.
At that moment, the Runecandels couldn't help but feel another shock.
Killing the four wraiths was no longer surprising, but the sword energy just
displayed was proof that Hedo had never shown his full strength before.
Also, his sword had a slight resemblance to Siron's realm, which completely 'annihilated' the target.
"Pass, Runecandels."
Amid the terrifying silence, Hedo finally spoke.
His longsword veil still emitted a dazzling light.
[Well, physical beauty. How about putting down the sword and talking if you're going to let us pass? Huh? It's not like you want to keep going. The kids are scared.]
"I don't think the courage of the Runecandels who confronted me so much is false, Murakan. If you're uncomfortable, I'll apologize."
[Well, you don't have to go that far.]
Murakan transformed into a human and stood next to Jin.
"Keep that sword safe. It seems to have something to do with this Murakan. Let's go, kid."
As Jin moved after putting away the knife around Sandra's neck, the rest of the group exchanged glances and followed.
Passing by Hedo and showing one's back was tantamount to a suicidal act, but Jin moved forward without making eye contact with him.
There was no fear at all that Hedo might swing his sword from behind.
There was no need to doubt that he was not a man to be taken lightly.
"If the heavens are on your side."
As Jin passed by his shoulder, Hedo spoke in a low, deep voice.
"That must be because your father has become the heavens themselves."
It was a story about coincidence and fate that had flowed favorably for Jin to an extent that was difficult for Hedo to understand now.
"I will tell my father that I learned a lesson from you."
"Miss Sandra."
"Why again!"
As Sandra turned her head irritably, Hedo gently smiled. Then, with his giant hand like that of a giant, he carefully fixed Sandra's clothes.
"Have a good time."
Hedo still believed that Jin couldn't escape with Sandra. It wasn't an easy task for him either.
Just as Jin acknowledged that Hedo wasn't a man to be taken lightly and simply passed by the longsword veil.
Hedo also believed that Jin wasn't a weak person who would somehow kidnap Sandra to the Sword Garden.
Sandra had only provided tremendous help to the Runecandels, and Jin knew that Hedo was just being considerate of her brief escapade.
Even if he was an enemy.
Insisting on using Sandra further here and being greedy would tarnish a kind of trust they shared as warriors.
"Well, okay."
"Don't lose a limb again to commemorate our meeting like last time. While you're playing, you might want to think about retrieving the things they stole."
Sandra snickered.

"Why take back what was given? It's not such a big fuss. I wonder if it's important what's mine and what's yours between a couple? I was a bit upset when Jin took that guy's neck instead of me last time."
"Is that so?"
"We're leaving, so Hedo, you better sort out the situation over there. In my opinion, that's more of a problem than the vault being robbed."
Sandra pointed to the sky on the other side with her finger. The warship Gruenil was, quite literally, sinking the frigates like a madman.
"Yes, understood. See you later, then."
With a single leap, Hedo's giant figure shrank to a tiny dot in an instant. He looked almost like a bullet as he rapidly charged toward the Sota Desert's airspace.
The Drakka dragons were getting closer and closer to Gruenil and the fleet.
As if the fierce battle that had just taken place was all a lie, a cool dawn breeze swept through the broken White Night Tower.
As Hedo disappeared, the Runecandels seemed to catch their breath as if they had just awoken from a nightmare. He was undoubtedly the worst and strongest enemy the riders had ever faced.
A feverishly hot determination filled the riders' hearts. Although they couldn't say their brotherly love was strong, they accurately read each other's emotions without speaking.
It was a firm resolve and determination to become stronger.
However, there was just one person, a Runecandel who was not a rider.
Yona had other thoughts. She had been sweating coldly since she had inflicted a serious injury on Hedo, enduring backlash and internal injuries.
"Sister, are you alright? The backlash...!"
Jin supported her with a worried voice.
"Excuse me?"
Yona pointed to Sandra with her trembling fingers.
"...Our youngest has a lover... it's this... noisy... rascal. A couple? Jin... Sir? I'll kill... them."
From the beginning, she didn't care about anything else, and only the affection Sandra showed to Jin was irritating enough to make her want to kill.
Sandra met Yona's cold and deep murderous intent with sparkling eyes.

"Oh my, little sister! Can I call you little sister? Look at me, you're very close with our Jin, right? I know, I know. Sandra knows everything. Just wait a moment, I'll help you quickly without pain!"
"Get... away, I'll kill..."
"It's not good to be in pain all the way to escape the Sota Desert, little sister. We still have a long way to go, don't we? Let me see. Where is the anesthetic?"
Everyone who saw this scene couldn't help but be speechless with incredulity.
Jin and the Runecandels left the White Night Tower like that.
